claim: Acyl-CoA binding domain-containing 7 (Acbd7) is a paralog gene of the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein.
source: Acyl-CoA binding domain-containing 7 (Acbd7) is a paralog gene of the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein in which single nucleotide polymorphism has recently been associated with obesity in humans.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by in silico analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: Single nucleotide polymorphism in Acbd7 has been associated with obesity in humans.
source: Acyl-CoA binding domain-containing 7 (Acbd7) is a paralog gene of the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein in which single nucleotide polymorphism has recently been associated with obesity in humans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and referenced to Comuzzie et al., 2012 in the introduction.

claim: A splice variant isoform of the Acbd7 mRNA is expressed and translated by some POMC neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus.
source: In this report, we provide converging evidence indicating that a splice variant isoform of the Acbd7 mRNA is expressed and translated by some POMC and GABAergic-neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1i,j.

claim: A splice variant isoform of the Acbd7 mRNA is expressed and translated by some GABAergic neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus.
source: In this report, we provide converging evidence indicating that a splice variant isoform of the Acbd7 mRNA is expressed and translated by some POMC and GABAergic-neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1m,n.

claim: The ARC ACBD7 isoform is produced and processed into a bioactive peptide referred to as nonadecaneuropeptide (NDN) in response to catabolic signals.
source: We have demonstrated that the ARC ACBD7 isoform was produced and processed into a bioactive peptide referred to as nonadecaneuropeptide (NDN) in response to catabolic signals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by MRM-MS data in Figure 1f and fasting/refeeding experiments in Figure 1o-s.

claim: NDN is a potent anorexigenic signal.
source: We have characterized NDN as a potent anorexigenic signal acting through an uncharacterized endozepine G protein-coupled receptor and subsequently via the melanocortin system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by food intake experiments shown in Figure 2a-d.

claim: NDN acts through an uncharacterized endozepine G protein-coupled receptor.
source: We have characterized NDN as a potent anorexigenic signal acting through an uncharacterized endozepine G protein-coupled receptor and subsequently via the melanocortin system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by pharmacological experiments with LV-1075 shown in Figure 3c.

claim: NDN acts via the melanocortin system.
source: We have characterized NDN as a potent anorexigenic signal acting through an uncharacterized endozepine G protein-coupled receptor and subsequently via the melanocortin system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with MC4R antagonist and MC4R knockout mice shown in Figure 4j,k.

claim: ACBD7-producing neurons participate in the hypothalamic leptin signalling pathway.
source: Our results suggest that ACBD7-producing neurons participate in the hypothalamic leptin signalling pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by leptin injection experiments shown in Figure 5a-d.

claim: ACBD7-producing neurons are involved in the hypothalamic control exerted on food intake and energy expenditure by the leptin-melanocortin pathway.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that ACBD7-producing neurons are involved in the hypothalamic control exerted on food intake and energy expenditure by the leptin-melanocortin pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments including food intake, energy expenditure, and leptin signaling studies.

claim: The arcuate nucleus (ARC) hosts proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP) / neuropeptide Y (NPY) - producing neurons.
source: Among all the hypothalamic nuclei, the arcuate nucleus (ARC), which hosts proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP) / neuropeptide (NPY) - producing neurons, has emerged as a prominent structure in the control of both food intake and energy expenditure (Krashes et al., 2013, Mayer and Belsham, 2009, Luquet et al., 2005, Gropp et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The ARC has emerged as a prominent structure in the control of both food intake and energy expenditure.
source: Among all the hypothalamic nuclei, the arcuate nucleus (ARC), which hosts proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP) / neuropeptide (NPY) - producing neurons, has emerged as a prominent structure in the control of both food intake and energy expenditure (Krashes et al., 2013, Mayer and Belsham, 2009, Luquet et al., 2005, Gropp et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: POMC and NPY/AgRP neurons are major constituents of the melanocortin system.
source: POMC and NPY/AgRP neurons are major constituents of the melanocortin system, which is recognized to genuinely govern energy balance regulation (Adan et al., 2006, Butler, 2006, Cone, 2006, De Jonghe et al., 2011, Ellacott and Cone, 2006, Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The melanocortin system is recognized to genuinely govern energy balance regulation.
source: POMC and NPY/AgRP neurons are major constituents of the melanocortin system, which is recognized to genuinely govern energy balance regulation (Adan et al., 2006, Butler, 2006, Cone, 2006, De Jonghe et al., 2011, Ellacott and Cone, 2006, Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: POMC neurons release α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), which induces hypophagic and thermogenic effects, mainly through the stimulation of the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R).
source: POMC neurons release α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), which induces hypophagic and thermogenic effects, mainly through the stimulation of the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) (Adan et al., 2006, Butler, 2006, Cone, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: AgRP has been described as an inverse agonist of the MC4R.
source: AgRP has been described as an inverse (Chai et al., 2003, Haskell-Luevano and Monck, 2001) or biased (Buch et al., 2009) agonist of this receptor.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: AgRP has been described as a biased agonist of the MC4R.
source: AgRP has been described as an inverse (Chai et al., 2003, Haskell-Luevano and Monck, 2001) or biased (Buch et al., 2009) agonist of this receptor.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Endozepines are described as glial endogenous peptides.
source: EZs are described as glial endogenous peptides (Tonon et al., 1990), which are derived from the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein (Dbi/Acbp) gene (Mogensen et al., 1987, Ferrero et al., 1984, Corda et al., 1984), and which include DBI/ACBP itself, the triakontatetraneuropeptide (TTN) and the octadecaneuropeptide (ODN).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Endozepines are derived from the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein (Dbi/Acbp) gene.
source: EZs are described as glial endogenous peptides (Tonon et al., 1990), which are derived from the diazepam-binding inhibitor/Acyl-CoA binding protein (Dbi/Acbp) gene (Mogensen et al., 1987, Ferrero et al., 1984, Corda et al., 1984), and which include DBI/ACBP itself, the triakontatetraneuropeptide (TTN) and the octadecaneuropeptide (ODN).

claim: Endozepines were initially characterized for their ability to displace benzodiazepines from their binding sites.
source: EZs were initially characterized for their ability to displace benzodiazepines from their binding sites (i.e. the γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor (GABAA-R) and the translocator protein (TSPO) (Ferrero et al., 1984, Slobodyansky et al., 1989).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The benzodiazepine binding sites include the γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor (GABAA-R) and the translocator protein (TSPO).

evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: ODN emerged as endogenous modulator of the brain melanocortin signalling pathway.
source: Recently, ODN emerged as endogenous modulator of the brain melanocortin signalling pathway and as a potential actor in the hypothalamic regulation of energy homeostasis (Lanfray et al., 2013), by acting via an uncharacterized G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) (do Rego et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: ODN is a potential actor in the hypothalamic regulation of energy homeostasis.
source: Recently, ODN emerged as endogenous modulator of the brain melanocortin signalling pathway and as a potential actor in the hypothalamic regulation of energy homeostasis (Lanfray et al., 2013), by acting via an uncharacterized G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) (do Rego et al., 2007).

evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: DBI/ACBP single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) was associated with obesity in humans.
source: Further supporting the role of Dbi/Acbp products in energy balance, a study conducted in humans by Comuzzie and collaborators (Comuzzie et al., 2012), indicates that DBI/ACBP single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) was associated with obesity, supporting the relevance of the DBI/ACBP production in energy homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: A SNP in ACBD7 was associated with obesity in humans.
source: Interestingly, Comuzzie and collaborators (Comuzzie et al., 2012) also identified a SNP in a well-conserved paralog gene of the DBI/ACBP, referred as Acyl-CoA binding domain containing 7 (ACBD7), as associated to obesity in humans (Comuzzie et al., 2012), suggesting that ACBD7 could be involved in energy homeostasis through encoding products related to EZs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The Acbd7 gene is a well-conserved paralog gene of the Dbi/Acbp.
source: In silico analysis indicates that the Acbd7 gene is a well-conserved paralog gene of the Dbi/Acbp (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b), that could also lead to the production of bioactive fragments in several vertebrate species, including human and rodent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in silico analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: The Acbd7 gene could lead to the production of bioactive fragments in several vertebrate species, including human and rodent.
source: In silico analysis indicates that the Acbd7 gene is a well-conserved paralog gene of the Dbi/Acbp (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b), that could also lead to the production of bioactive fragments in several vertebrate species, including human and rodent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in silico analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b,c.

claim: The prevalent Acbd7 mRNA sequence in the murine brain differs from that already described (Acbd7-001) in the NCBI database.
source: We first verified the sequence of Acbd7 mRNA in the murine brain and demonstrated a prevalent sequence (Figure 1a) that differs from that already described (Acbd7-001) in the NCBI database (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/NM_030063.2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The observed splice variant contained 3 additional nucleotides at the splice junction of exons 2 and 3.
source: The observed splice variant contained 3 additional nucleotides at the splice junction of exons 2 and 3, (Figure 1a), thereby predicting the insertion of a single glycine between the Ile43 and Ala44 of the originally expected 88-amino acid-encoded ACBD7-001 protein (herewith referred as ACBD788—Figure 1—figure supplement 1d) and the production of a 89-amino acid-containing protein isoform (herewith referred as ACBD789).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The splice variant predicts the insertion of a single glycine between the Ile43 and Ala44 of the originally expected 88-amino acid-encoded ACBD7-001 protein.

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Acbd7 mRNA is present in the ARC.

claim: Hypothalamic cells can process ACBD789 into a 19-amino-acid fragment (ACBD789 (34-52)) named nonadecaneuropeptide (NDN).

claim: Western blot experiments revealed the presence in the mediobasal hypothalamus (MBH) of a single band of 10 kDa.
source: Western blot experiments, using immuno-purified ACBD7 specific antibody, revealed the presence in the mediobasal hypothalamus (MBH) of a single band of 10 kDa, (Figure 1d), confirming that ACBD7 was endogenously produced in the MBH.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: ACBD7 is endogenously produced in the MBH.
source: Western blot experiments, using immuno-purified ACBD7 specific antibody, revealed the presence in the mediobasal hypothalamus (MBH) of a single band of 10 kDa, (Figure 1d), confirming that ACBD7 was endogenously produced in the MBH.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Endogenous NDN was found in the hypothalamic lysates.
source: This protocol performed on mice MBH extracts, using synthetic NDN as control (Figure 1e), indicated that endogenous NDN was found in the hypothalamic lysates (Figure 1f), thus confirming that the ACBD789 isoform is produced but also processed in the mouse brain.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by MRM-MS data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The ACBD789 isoform is produced and processed in the mouse brain.

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by MRM-MS data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: ACBD7 labelling was not observed without colchicine or 3-methyladenin (3-MA) pre-treatment.
source: Immunohistochemical analysis performed using the ACBD7-specific antibody revealed that ACBD7 labelling was not observed without colchicine or 3-methyladenin (3-MA) pre-treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: ACBD7 was not stained in glial cells (GFAP) in the MBH.
source: Double immunostaining performed on brain sections of colchicine-treated mice revealed that ACBD7 was not stained in glial cells (GFAP) in the MBH (Figure 1g,h).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1g,h.

claim: ACBD7 was stained in some ARC POMC neurons.
source: We also observed that ACBD7 was stained in some ARC POMC neurons (Figure 1i,j) and some vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) positive neurons (Figure 1m,n) in 3-MA-treated mice, indicating that ACBD7 is predominantly produced by neurons in the MBH.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1i,j.

claim: ACBD7 was stained in some vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) positive neurons.
source: We also observed that ACBD7 was stained in some ARC POMC neurons (Figure 1i,j) and some vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) positive neurons (Figure 1m,n) in 3-MA-treated mice, indicating that ACBD7 is predominantly produced by neurons in the MBH.

claim: No apparent ACBD7 staining was observed in NPY neurons.
source: However, investigation performed on colchicine-treated mice revealed no apparent ACBD7 staining in NPY neurons (Figure 1k,l).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1k,l.

claim: 18 hr of fasting reduced Acbd7 mRNA levels in the ARC of control mice by about 50%.
source: We observed that 18 hr of fasting was sufficient to reduce Acbd7 mRNA levels in the ARC of control mice by about 50%, whereas refeeding (2h) restored Acbd7 expression (Figure 1o).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1o.

claim: Refeeding (2h) restored Acbd7 expression in the ARC.
source: We observed that 18 hr of fasting was sufficient to reduce Acbd7 mRNA levels in the ARC of control mice by about 50%, whereas refeeding (2h) restored Acbd7 expression (Figure 1o).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1o.

claim: No effect of fasting or refeeding challenge was observed on Acbd7 mRNA levels in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN).
source: Notably, no effect of fasting or even refeeding challenge was observed on Acbd7 mRNA levels in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) (Figure 1p).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1p.

claim: Refeeding (6h) increased the protein levels of ACBD7 by about 3 times.
source: Additionally, western blot analysis performed on MBH extract using fasted mice as controls, indicated that refeeding (6h) increased the protein levels of ACBD7 by about 3 times (Figure 1q,r), suggesting that both Acbd7 mRNA and ACBD7 protein levels in the ARC correlated with the body energy status.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1q,r.

claim: Both Acbd7 mRNA and ACBD7 protein levels in the ARC correlated with the body energy status.
source: Additionally, western blot analysis performed on MBH extract using fasted mice as controls, indicated that refeeding (6h) increased the protein levels of ACBD7 by about 3 times (Figure 1q,r), suggesting that both Acbd7 mRNA and ACBD7 protein levels in the ARC correlated with the body energy status.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization and Western blot data shown in Figure 1o-r.

claim: The MBH levels of NDN increased 2 fold after 2 hr of refeeding.
source: Consistently with our previous results, the MBH levels of NDN increased 2 fold after 2 hr of refeeding (Figure 1s), suggesting that production of ACBD789 and its processing into NDN was influenced by the energy status.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by MRM-MS data shown in Figure 1s.

claim: Production of ACBD789 and its processing into NDN was influenced by the energy status.

claim: All injected compounds (NDN, ACBD788 (34-51), and NDN(12-19)) led to anorexigenic effects that were seen as early as 30 min after injection.
source: We observed that all injected compounds led to anorexigenic effects that were seen as early as 30 min after injection.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2a-c.

claim: The optimal concentrations to cause hypophagia differed for each peptide (NDN, ACBD788 (34-51), and NDN(12-19)).
source: However, dose/response experiments indicate that the optimal concentrations to cause hypophagia differed for each peptide (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: A potent inhibition of food intake was observed in mice administrated with 10 ng (5.1 10–12 mol) of NDN.
source: Indeed, a potent inhibition of food intake was observed in mice administrated with 10 ng (5.1 10–12 mol) of NDN (Figure 2a), while this effect was only achieved when 100 ng (5.3 10–11 mol) of the ACBD788 (34-51) fragment were icv-injected (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Inhibition of food intake was only achieved when 100 ng (5.3 10–11 mol) of the ACBD788 (34-51) fragment were icv-injected.

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: NDN(12-19) was efficient for doses as low as 5 ng (5.6 10–12 mol).

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The biological activity of the ACBD7-derived peptides is ensured by the C-terminal octapeptide NDN(12-19).
source: Consistently, NDN(12-19), the common C-terminal octapeptide of ACBD788 (34-51) and NDN was efficient for doses as low as 5 ng (5.6 10–12 mol) (Figure 2c), suggesting that the biological activity of the ACBD7-derived peptides is ensured by this well-conserved fragment.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The anorexigenic effect induced by NDN(12-19) was not present 24 hr after the icv injection.
source: Furthermore, we observed that the anorexigenic effect induced by NDN(12-19) was not present 24 hr after the icv injection (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by food intake data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: NDN and NDN(12-19) are both 10 times more potent than ACBD788 (34-51), in reducing food intake by 50%.
source: Interestingly, comparison of the efficiency of each peptide, 3 hr after injection, revealed that NDN as well as NDN(12-19) are both 10 times more potent than ACBD788 (34-51), in reducing food intake by 50% (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: NDN increased the energy expenditure in mice.
source: NDN increased the energy expenditure in mice (Figure 2e,f), while increasing the O2 consumption (Figure 2g) and CO2 production (Figure 2h), without affecting the respiratory quotient (Figure 2i) or the physical activity pattern (Figure 2j), over 6 hr following the icv injection.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by indirect calorimetry data shown in Figure 2e,f.

claim: NDN increased O2 consumption in mice.
